A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same LobbyLens legislative-deception study. All 18 pages of v2 and 24 pages of v3, including appendices, were readable; text extraction and rendered figures supported reliable matching.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLM simulations, identification and benefit-capture measurements, human evaluations, prompt robustness tests, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and reports additional critic configurations, negative controls, and manual analysis of deception strategies.

M1.justification: v3 Appendix A.3 adds a critic variant that polls three LLMs' pairwise decisions before ranking candidates. The core objectives, generation procedure, and appendix prompts remain substantially unchanged under the renamed re-planning/re-sampling terminology. Conflicting feedback-source descriptions in Section 4.1 and Appendix C.3 do not establish a further change to the core loop.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 936 bills and 4,439 bill-company pairs, with unchanged legislative and company coverage. v3 Section 5 adds limited test scenarios involving unrelated bill/business/amendment combinations and bill-only inputs, extending evaluation to cases without relevant generated amendments.

E2.justification: v3 adds weaker-critic comparisons and a pooled Qwen 14B, Mixtral, and Yi 34B critic. The original stronger-critic comparisons remain. v2 Table 9's separate without-critique comparator disappears; v3 Figure 5 instead reports a Qwen 14B comparison with and without re-planning, related to the earlier reflection ablation.

E3.justification: The evaluation design expands through weaker and pooled critic configurations, randomly mismatched and amendment-omission controls on 10% of the dataset, and a new 25-sample manual strategy-coding study. The no-concealment condition is also reported across three trials. These are additional protocols; the original corpus, principal metrics, and 100-simulation human evaluation remain.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses of critic strength and aggregation, metric behavior without relevant amendments, re-planning versus resampling, and three linguistic deception strategies. It removes v2's separate Mixtral critique/reflection ablations and policy-area breakdown. The state/Squire analysis and CoT analysis are retained in Appendix A, rather than newly added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations from 10,000 bootstrap iterations and retain the 75.3% human agreement figure. No changed seed policy, repeated-run count, confidence-interval procedure, or significance-testing method is documented. Additional result entries do not establish a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New results include weaker/pooled critics, 24.08% identification on mismatched inputs, and the 81.8% cross-benefit-diversion frequency. Policy-area and separate component-ablation results disappear. Most original scores remain, including Tables 2–4 and 6–8, but Table 5's no-concealment score changes from 78.1 to 79.1. v3 Section 5 also reverses Qwen 7B's trial sequence to 70.9, 73.5, 85.8, contradicting the retained Table 7 sequence of 85.8, 73.5, 70.9.

T1.justification: v3's introduction adds an explicit generalized definition involving n message objectives, k concealed self-serving objectives, and the remaining emphasized objectives. The dataset-selection inequality, critic criterion, and constrained optimization objective in Equations 1–3 remain unchanged. No new proofs or theorems appear.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly centers technically truthful strategic phrasing and adds the identification of recurring deception strategies to its main contributions. The underlying legislative testbed, LobbyLens dataset, and claim that iterative refinement increases deception by approximately 40 percentage points remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations of target-service abstraction, regulation-to-business abstraction, and cross-benefit diversion. Its limitations newly explain the simplified legislative model, possible simultaneous public and private benefits, limited GPT-4 evaluation, and absence of human validation of benefactor identification. The earlier cognitive-load interpretation of model-size effects is removed.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a code-and-dataset access link where v2 promised future dataset release. It identifies the existing human evaluators as in-house AI experts and describes author participation and legal guidance for the new strategy analysis. Dataset construction, constrained decoding, GGUF/llama.cpp usage, and reported computing budgets are retained.

R1.justification: v3 substantially revises positioning through legislative-lobbying literature and newer work on manipulation, persuasion, sleeper agents, and hidden-objective auditing. It explicitly distinguishes black-box strategic phrasing from these settings. The communication/cognitive-science discussion and associated citations, including Searle, Buller and Burgoon, and Sarkadi, are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and method narrative are extensively rewritten, including systematic replacement of verbal-reinforcement terminology. v3 adds a conclusion and acknowledgments and reorganizes the appendices into Additional Results, Design Decisions, and Simulations with numbered subsections and a contents page.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn as a horizontal workflow. v3 adds a strategy radar chart and several critic/ablation plots, restructures the main critic comparison, and relocates the original stronger-critic and state plots to Appendix A. The policy-area figure and separate ablation table disappear, and document typography and prompt formatting change throughout.

improvement.justification: v3's negative controls, additional critic tests, and manual strategy analysis provide useful validation and explanatory evidence. The access link and explicit limitations improve reproducibility and appropriately bound the legislative case study. The net gain is limited: principal results remain unchanged, separate component ablations are lost, and the rewritten model-size discussion introduces a trial-order error contradicted by Table 7.
